summary: AE + SE walkthrough of Redwood SDK quickstarts (Python/TypeScript), auth setup, and environment config. Focus on hosted vs Dedicated options, VPC/private deployment notes, and benchmark planning. Customer asked about KMS, SOC2, latency/cost trade-offs and CI/CD best practices for rollout. Agreed next steps: share quickstart repo, pricing, and schedule benchmark window.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Alex from Redwood, with Priya our solutions eng. quick roll call?
[00:05] Janelle Park (Aurora): Janelle here, marco and leah are on as well. we got about 45 minutes, thanks.
[00:12] Alex Chen (Redwood): awesome, objective for today is a hands-on SDK integration walkthrough — python and typescript quickstarts, auth, env setup and then a quick convo about prod options (hosted, dedicated, private) and benching. sound good?
[00:20] Marco Ruiz (Aurora): yeah that's perfect. we mostly want to see the dev ergonomics; our engs will implement in node and py. also need notes on data residency and KMS.
[00:28] Priya Desai (Redwood SE): great. i'll share my screen in a sec, but first quick qual: what does your stack look like? kubernetes? cloud? are you on GCP?
[00:35] Leah Kim (Aurora DevOps): we're on GCP, GKE, private clusters behind a NAT, we use Cloud KMS and have strict egress rules.
[00:42] Janelle Park (CTO): infra team wants either VPC peering or a private deployment, timeline is wanting a pilot in 6-8 weeks.
[00:50] Alex Chen (Redwood): perfect, those are common. ok Priya over to you for the quickstart run.
[00:55] Priya Desai (Redwood SE): cool. i'm opening the quickstart repo link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (note: shared link in chat). first example is python - pip install redwood-sdk, set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var. example: from redwood import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']); resp = client.generate("Write a short summary of order #1234").
[01:18] Marco Ruiz (Aurora): open question: how do you do auth for service accounts? we use GCP service accounts for CI.
[01:23] Priya Desai (Redwood SE): good q. we support API keys for service-to-service; for enterprise we also support OIDC + SAML for token exchange and short-lived credentials. for Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your IdP and KMS for key wrapping.
[01:40] Janelle Park (Aurora): and for the hosted option, keys stored server-side, encrypted?
[01:45] Alex Chen (Redwood): yep hosted API keys are encrypted at rest, keys rotate, and you can integrate with your KMS for customer-managed keys on Private. we'll share SOC2 and KMS integration docs.
[01:55] Priya Desai (Redwood SE): switching to TS quickstart: npm i @redwood-inference/sdk; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); const resp = await client.chat.create({ messages: [...] }) — we show streaming via server-sent events in the example. note some transcriptions call it Redwood Optimiz in the docs, ignore that typo.
[02:18] Marco Ruiz (Aurora): about environment setup — we have local dev, CI, and your recommended prod: what's best practice for secrets and rotating keys?
[02:25] Priya Desai (Redwood SE): best practice: store short-lived keys in CI using secret manager, rotate keys monthly, and in prod use either Dedicated with private networking or Private (VPC) deployment. for hosted calls we recommend using a proxy in your VPC to avoid open egress to internet if that's a blocker.
[02:35] Leah Kim (Aurora): do you support VPC peering or private link?
[02:38] Alex Chen (Redwood): yes — Redwood Private supports VPC peering and private backbone. Dedicated has options for private network peering and can be configured to only accept traffic from your IP ranges. we'll document the exact patterns.
[02:47] Marco Ruiz (Aurora): one more infra -- latency: for token-heavy responses we care about < 150ms p95 per token generation ideally; can you comment?
[02:54] Priya Desai (Redwood SE): latency depends on model and sequence length. with our runtime, q4 models on A100-equivalent have typical per-token latency of 80-120ms in hosted region; Dedicated can be tuned (batching, quantization) to hit lower p95s. caching (prefix/KV cache) helps a lot for repeated prompts. note: some folks call it K-V cash in notes, ha.
[03:15] Janelle Park (Aurora): we also need to understand cost — we'd likely start on hosted and potentially move to Dedicated for predictable unit cost. what's the migration path?
[03:22] Alex Chen (Redwood): straightforward — same API and SDK. you pin model versions and rollout policies via the Console. live traffic can be shifted to Dedicated pools with canary deploys. Redwood Console shows per-route token costs so you can measure delta before commit.
[03:33] Marco Ruiz (Aurora): did you mention quantization profiles? our models will be open models, probably quantized 4-bit.
[03:38] Priya Desai (Redwood SE): yes — Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization and kernel profiles per workload. we support 4-bit quantization and do compatibility checks for accuracy regressions. we'll include a short report template to evaluate quality vs cost.
[03:50] Alex Chen (Redwood): security — SOC 2, ISO, SSO, audit logs, retention. quick question: do you need auditable request logs in your SSO scope?
03:58] Janelle Park (Aurora): yes, need full audit trails for data access. and logs must be stored for 12 months.
[04:04] Alex Chen (Redwood): ok we support audit logs, retention is configurable for Dedicated/Private. hosted has standard retention but we can discuss enterprise add-on for longer retention. will share the security pack.
[04:12] Priya Desai (Redwood SE): demo time: walking through the python quickstart in the repo. i'll paste the snippet we usually use for CI: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret="aurora-redwood-api"); pytest tests/test_integration.py -k smoke. locally you can run with a dev key.
[04:30] Marco Ruiz (Aurora): will the SDK work behind our corporate proxy? sometimes streaming breaks with our proxy.
[04:36] Priya Desai (Redwood SE): yes we have guidance. streaming via SSE sometimes needs proxy tweaks; we have a fallback polling client in the SDK. we'll include config in the quickstart README.
[04:48] Alex Chen (Redwood): benchmarks — to make benching meaningful we need sample traffic patterns (qps, token lengths, concurrency). Marco, can you share a couple payload examples?
[04:55] Marco Ruiz (Aurora): yes, i'll drop sample payloads and our 2-week traffic window.
[04:58] Priya Desai (Redwood SE): perfect, we'll plan a bench in a staging project; recommended pattern is run 3x: cold start, warmed KV cache, and warmed with batching.
[05:10] Leah Kim (Aurora): on compliance, if we go Private on-prem, do you support offline deployment?
[05:14] Alex Chen (Redwood): yes offline/air-gapped options exist; private on-prem package includes KMS integrations and offline install docs. we'll coordinate SRE runbook with your infra.
[05:22] Priya Desai (Redwood SE): returning to code briefly, here's a snippet for TypeScript streaming fallback: // if SSE blocked, set client.stream=false and poll client.chat.fetch(id) every 200ms. we put this in the samples.
[05:36] Janelle Park (Aurora): curious about rate limits, quotas — we have bursty traffic from event replays. how does Redwood handle burst capacity?
[05:43] Alex Chen (Redwood): Dedicated pools can be configured with burst capacity and autoscaling. hosted has soft rate limits and we can set per-account quotas to avoid noisy neighbors. for critical paths we recommend Dedicated with reserved throughput.
[05:55] Marco Ruiz (Aurora): any known compatibility issues with GKE private clusters?
[05:58] Priya Desai (Redwood SE): none in general; common blockers are egress rules and DNS resolution for streaming endpoints. we provide a small sidecar proxy example in the quickstart for that exact scenario.
[06:12] Alex Chen (Redwood): ok quick recap: we'll share quickstart repo, include the python and ts snippets, proxy sidecar example, and the security pack (SOC2, KMS guide). Alex to send pricing and Dedicated options; Priya to share bench playbook and sample scripts. Marco to send payloads and traffic windows. schedule bench for next week if possible.
[06:30] Janelle Park (Aurora): that works. last question: how long to onboard to Dedicated if we choose that path?
[06:36] Alex Chen (Redwood): typically 4-6 weeks from purchase to initial pass if network and infra approvals are quick; Private on-prem takes longer depending on approvals.
[06:44] Leah Kim (Aurora): ok thanks, also please include runbook for key rotation.
[06:48] Priya Desai (Redwood SE): will do.
[06:51] Alex Chen (Redwood): great, i'll follow up with an email with the links and next steps. thanks everyone.
[06:55] Transcript notes: occasional transcription artifacts (Redwood Optimiz, K-V cash) and speaker mis-ids. references shared: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts, security pack (link sent after call), pricing spreadsheet (will be sent).
[07:10] End of recording.
